name: The DeSoto Oak

location.address: Plant Park, University Drive, University of Tampa, Tampa, FL 33606

access: Free. Plant Park is the open grounds beside Plant Hall (University of Tampa campus) on the Hillsborough River; the oak stands on University Drive with a DAR plaque at its foot. Walk-up from the sidewalk.
transport: Downtown Tampa; TECO Line Streetcar and the Riverwalk are a short walk away (about 10 minutes on foot from the Straz Center / Kennedy Blvd side). Not timed by the pass.
verify_notes: Plant Museum (Henry B. Plant Museum, occupies Plant Hall on UT's campus; publishes the park history): 'Early Tampa residents claimed that this majestic live oak, The DeSoto Oak, was standing well before the hotel was built' (Tampa Bay Hotel opened 1891, so the claim is only 'older than 1891' by local recollection, no measured age). The Spanish explorer legend (bargaining with Native Americans under it) is tradition; the DAR plaque itself says 'tradition says'. Plaque text per Waymarking: 'This tablet erected by De Soto Chapter DAR marks the tree under which tradition says De Soto parlayed with the Indians.' Waymarking coordinate N 27 56.775 W 082 27.830 is the plaque stone 'located under the old oak', hence the pin; precision is about 2 m, so treated as a GPS-at-the-tree position. Early-20th-century postcards (USF Digital Commons, Hampton Dunn collection records dunn_postcards/3949, 3950, 3951) show a large live oak in the grounds; not checked that postcard tree is this exact trunk. NO age basis: do not bridge to 1539 or to 1891. No girth, height or register. Alive: lifecheck RECENT, iNaturalist observation 411446834 dated 2026-10-28 within range (not confirmed to be this trunk); no storm-loss report found for the oak after Hurricane Milton (UT reported no significant campus damage, Minaret 2024-11-20). One-source basis (ground owner) plus plaque. Which trunk: this is the named one; Plant Park also holds many other planted oaks and Anton Fiehe's palm walk (1890s planting, not tied to this tree). A transplanted 65 ft, 36 in oak (UT award 2012) and two oaks moved in 2000 are different trees.
story:
The plaque at the foot of this oak is unusually honest. The De Soto Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution put it there to mark the tree "under which tradition says De Soto parlayed with the Indians." Tradition says. The plaque claims no more than that, and neither do we.

What can be said is smaller and still worth the walk. Early Tampa residents remembered the oak standing before the Tampa Bay Hotel was built beside it, and the hotel opened in 1891. That is local memory rather than a measurement. It makes the tree older than the hotel, if the memory is right, and says nothing more precise. Nobody has published an age, a girth or a height for it. If you know any of them, tell us.

Plant Park is the open ground beside Plant Hall on the University of Tampa campus, running down to the Hillsborough River, and the Henry B. Plant Museum keeps its history. The park is full of planted oaks and has a palm walk from the 1890s, so the plaque is what picks this one out. Postcards from the early twentieth century show a large live oak in these grounds, though nobody has checked that it is this trunk.

No report of storm damage to it followed Hurricane Milton in 2024. Entry is free, straight off the pavement on University Drive, and the TECO Line Streetcar and the Riverwalk are about ten minutes away on foot.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the DAR plaque on a stone at its foot, the one that mentions De Soto. It stands on University Drive in Plant Park, beside Plant Hall on the University of Tampa campus.
